paper.title_en: Probing spin dynamics in MnSi under pressure by energy-integrated time-of-flight small-angle neutron scattering
paper.abstract_en: We demonstrate that energy-integrated time-of-flight small-angle neutron scattering can determine the long-wavelength spin-wave stiffness of field-polarized MnSi inside a pressure cell. A forward model maps neutron energy loss and gain into the recorded time-of-flight coordinates, allowing a joint fit of radial profiles in several apparent-wavelength windows to constrain a common stiffness. Ambient-pressure powder and polycrystal measurements reproduce the established stiffness scale of MnSi. At effective pressures of 3.5 and 7.8 kbar, the fitted stiffness spans 43--61 meV $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}^2$ across the measured states and is comparable in magnitude to the scale inferred from the helical wave vector and applied upper critical field. The characteristic SANS ordering temperature decreases from 28.8 K at ambient pressure to 17.4 K at 7.8 kbar. The long-wavelength gradient stiffness alone therefore does not account for the pressure evolution of helimagnetic ordering. These results demonstrate a route to quantitative studies of spin-wave dynamics under pressure on time-of-flight SANS instruments without final-energy analysis.
